docs.title: Smart UI Focus & Navigation
docs.text:
Reliable controller & keyboard focus for Unity uGUI.

Keep your existing Unity uGUI menu system. Add reliable keyboard/gamepad focus and smarter directional navigation without replacing your UI framework, EventSystem, or Input System UI module.

Compatible with Unity 2022.3 LTS and Unity 6. Validated with Built-in, URP, and HDRP.

The included Focus Management sample demonstrates the complete runtime workflow in a focused uGUI scene.

docs.title: What it providesFocus lifecycleMenu continuityInput awarenessDirectional control
docs.text:
Recover invalid selection and resolve a configured default or valid descendant when keyboard or gamepad focus is needed.

Remember selection per scope and restore the exact prior control after a modal closes when it remains valid.

Observe Mouse, Keyboard, and Gamepad UI activity through the New Input System without replacing Unity's input module.

Generate bounds-aware links for freeform and structured layouts, with explicit per-direction overrides when required.

Unity's built-in navigation remains suitable for many ordinary menus. Smart UI Focus & Navigation is intended for projects that need more control over focus lifecycle, structured layouts, and directional edge cases while continuing to use standard uGUI Selectable components.

docs.title: Start here
docs.text:
1. Review Requirements & Compatibility, then follow installation.
  2. Follow the getting started guide.
  3. Open the included sample scene.

For detailed behavior, see focus management, input modes, and smart navigation.

docs.title: API reference
docs.text:
All public runtime types use the namespace:

LevelArgento.SmartUINavigation

docs.title: 1.0.0 — Initial release
docs.text:
• Reliable default focus and invalid-selection recovery for uGUI menus.
  • Per-scope remembered selection.
  • Modal push/pop focus restoration.
  • Mouse, keyboard, and gamepad input-mode detection using the New Input System.
  • Bounds-aware directional navigation generation for uGUI Selectables.
  • Freeform, VerticalList, HorizontalList, and Grid layout topologies.
  • Ragged-grid row and column boundary handling.
  • Auto, None, and Explicit per-direction overrides.
  • Automatic and explicit rebuild support for dynamic UI.
  • Focus management and dynamic navigation sample scene.

docs.title: Dynamic UI
docs.text:
SmartNavigationGroup supports common runtime changes without rebuilding continuously when nothing has changed.

With Rebuild Automatically enabled, it detects or receives dirty signals for:

  • added and removed Selectable controls;
  • hierarchy and sibling-order changes;
  • active/inactive changes;
  • enabled/disabled changes;
  • interactable changes;
  • RectTransform size, transform, and layout changes; and
  • layout-constraint or override changes.
Your browser does not support embedded video. Open the dynamic navigation demonstration. Runtime additions, removals, disabled items, reordering, and list/grid changes rebuild against the updated layout.

The group checks relevant observed state before canvas rendering and rebuilds only when dirty or changed. This monitoring has a runtime cost; it is not described as zero-cost.

docs.title: Preferred deferred rebuild
docs.text:
For a VerticalLayoutGroup, HorizontalLayoutGroup, or GridLayoutGroup, mark both the layout and navigation dirty after changing content:

using LevelArgento.SmartUINavigation;
using UnityEngine;
using UnityEngine.UI;

public sealed class DynamicMenu : MonoBehaviour
{
    [SerializeField] private RectTransform content;
    [SerializeField] private SmartNavigationGroup navigationGroup;

    public void ContentChanged()
    {
        LayoutRebuilder.MarkLayoutForRebuild(content);
        navigationGroup.MarkNavigationDirty();
    }
}

With automatic rebuilding enabled, Unity updates the layout and the group rebuilds before a later canvas render.

docs.title: Immediate rebuild
docs.text:
When links are required synchronously in the same call, force the relevant layout first:

LayoutRebuilder.ForceRebuildLayoutImmediate(content);
navigationGroup.RebuildNavigation();

Use this only when immediate results are required. For custom asynchronous transitions or layout animation, call the rebuild after final RectTransform positions are available.

docs.title: Automatic rebuilding disabled
docs.text: MarkNavigationDirty() records the dirty state but does not rebuild while RebuildAutomatically is false. Call RebuildNavigation() explicitly after layout settles.

docs.title: Removed controls
docs.text:
Rebuilding stops removed or invalid controls from being targets of current participants. A removed control may retain the explicit navigation previously written to its own Selectable, because it is no longer part of the group being rebuilt. Clear or replace that control's navigation if it will be reused elsewhere.

If the selected control becomes invalid during a content change, SmartFocusManager can recover selection within the active focus scope according to its configured input-mode policy.

docs.title: Focus management
docs.text: SmartFocusManager coordinates the active menu scope. SmartFocusScope defines which descendant Selectable controls belong to that menu and optionally remembers the last valid selection.

docs.title: Focus target precedence
docs.text:
When a scope needs focus, its target is resolved in this order:

remembered selection
        ↓
default selection
        ↓
first valid descendant Selectable

A valid target must belong to the active scope and be active, enabled, and interactable. An invalid remembered or default selection is skipped.

docs.title: SmartFocusManager
docs.text:
Configure these Inspector fields:

  • Event System: the managed EventSystem. If empty, the manager resolves EventSystem.current.
  • Initial Scope: the scope focused when the manager starts.
  • Input Mode Detector: optional mode source used to pause automatic recovery during mouse-driven interaction.
  • Recover Invalid Selection: restores a valid focus target when the current selection becomes invalid.
A manager can reference the EventSystem, initial scope, and optional input-mode detector explicitly.

The main runtime operations are:

  • SetScope(scope) changes the active scope and resolves focus immediately.
  • RequestFocus(selectable) selects a specific valid control in the current scope.
  • RecoverFocus() resolves the normal remembered/default/fallback sequence on demand.
  • PushModal(scope) and PopModal() manage modal focus restoration.

SetScope(null) stops scope monitoring without changing the current EventSystem selection. Every SetScope call also clears pending modal restoration history; use PushModal and PopModal for modal flows.

docs.title: SmartFocusScope
docs.text:
Set Default Selection to the control that should receive focus when the scope has no valid memory. Remember Last Selection is enabled by default. Disable it when every entry should start from the default or first valid descendant.

Each scope defines its own default and selection-memory policy.

Call ClearRememberedSelection() to discard stored selection explicitly:

optionsScope.ClearRememberedSelection();
focusManager.SetScope(optionsScope);

The remembered object is used only while it remains a valid descendant of the scope.

docs.title: Invalid-selection recovery
docs.text:
While a scope is active, the manager observes the EventSystem selection. With recovery enabled, it can replace a selection that is:

  • missing;
  • outside the current scope;
  • on an inactive GameObject;
  • on a disabled Selectable; or
  • non-interactable.

When an active SmartInputModeDetector is assigned, automatic recovery pauses in Mouse mode. Keyboard or gamepad UI activity can restore valid focus when needed. Without an active detector, recovery remains enabled regardless of pointer activity.

Your browser does not support embedded video. Open the focus recovery demonstration. Focus remains usable as the sample moves between pointer and keyboard-driven interaction.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text: This setup adds default focus, selection memory, and invalid-selection recovery to an existing uGUI menu.

docs.title: Configure the scene
docs.text:
1. Ensure the scene contains one active EventSystem with InputSystemUIInputModule.
  2. Add SmartFocusManager to a scene object and assign the EventSystem.
  3. Add SmartFocusScope to the root of a menu or panel.
  4. Assign a valid child Selectable to Default Selection.
  5. Leave Remember Last Selection enabled if returning to the menu should restore its last valid selection.
  6. Assign the scope to the manager's Initial Scope, or call SetScope when the menu opens.
  7. For mouse-aware focus recovery, add SmartInputModeDetector, assign its UI action references, and assign the detector to the manager.
  8. Enter Play Mode and test with keyboard and gamepad navigation.

The scope and its default control must be active when focus is requested.

docs.title: Switching menus from code
docs.text:
using LevelArgento.SmartUINavigation;
using UnityEngine;

public sealed class MenuController : MonoBehaviour
{
    [SerializeField] private SmartFocusManager focusManager;
    [SerializeField] private GameObject optionsPanel;
    [SerializeField] private SmartFocusScope optionsScope;

    public void OpenOptions()
    {
        optionsPanel.SetActive(true);
        focusManager.SetScope(optionsScope);
    }

    public void CloseOptions()
    {
        focusManager.SetScope(null);
        optionsPanel.SetActive(false);
    }
}

SetScope(null) stops monitoring a scope but does not itself clear or change the EventSystem selection. If another menu opens, activate it and call SetScope with its scope.

docs.title: Requesting a specific selection
docs.text:
using LevelArgento.SmartUINavigation;
using UnityEngine;
using UnityEngine.UI;

public sealed class FocusShortcut : MonoBehaviour
{
    [SerializeField] private SmartFocusManager focusManager;
    [SerializeField] private Button target;

    public void FocusTarget()
    {
        focusManager.RequestFocus(target);
    }
}

RequestFocus returns false if the target is outside the current scope, inactive, disabled, or non-interactable.

docs.title: Optional smart navigation
docs.text: For menus that need generated directional links, add SmartNavigationGroup to a common ancestor of the participating controls. It rebuilds after layout and hierarchy changes by default. See smart navigation before applying it to an existing navigation setup, because rebuilding writes Navigation.Mode.Explicit links.

docs.title: Input modes
docs.text: SmartInputModeDetector reports which device category most recently produced relevant UI activity.

docs.title: Modes
docs.text:
SmartInputMode contains:

  • Mouse
  • Keyboard
  • Gamepad

Read the current value through CurrentMode. Subscribe to ModeChanged when other presentation or focus code needs to respond:

using LevelArgento.SmartUINavigation;
using UnityEngine;

public sealed class InputModeStatus : MonoBehaviour
{
    [SerializeField] private SmartInputModeDetector detector;

    private void OnEnable()
    {
        detector.ModeChanged += OnModeChanged;
        OnModeChanged(detector.CurrentMode);
    }

    private void OnDisable()
    {
        detector.ModeChanged -= OnModeChanged;
    }

    private static void OnModeChanged(SmartInputMode mode)
    {
        Debug.Log($"UI input mode: {mode}");
    }
}

The event is raised only when the mode changes.

The detector observes the same navigation, submit, cancel, point, and click actions used by the UI module.

docs.title: Action configuration
docs.text:
Assign the detector's navigation, submit, cancel, pointer-position, and click references from the UI action map used by InputSystemUIInputModule. Those actions must be enabled by the input module or project code. The detector does not manage action lifetime.

Keyboard navigation, submit, or cancel activity selects Keyboard mode. Gamepad navigation, submit, or cancel activity selects Gamepad mode. Mouse movement meeting or exceeding the configured pixel threshold, or a mouse click, selects Mouse mode.

For gamepad navigation, the detector reads the action's processed Vector2. Keep the same navigation action and processors used by the UI module. A stick value removed by the action's deadzone remains zero and does not count as intentional navigation.

docs.title: Focus policy
docs.text:
When assigned to SmartFocusManager, Mouse mode prevents automatic recovery from unnecessarily forcing selection back onto a Selectable during pointer interaction. Relevant keyboard or gamepad activity can restore a valid focus target if the current selection is invalid.

This is a focused policy for uGUI selection recovery. It does not define every possible hover, cursor, or mixed-input presentation rule for an application.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Review Requirements & Compatibility before importing. The package requires Unity UI (com.unity.ugui) and the Unity Input System (com.unity.inputsystem).

Compatible with Unity 2022.3 LTS and Unity 6. Validated with Built-in, URP, and HDRP.

docs.title: Import
docs.text:
Import the asset into the Unity project through the Asset Store package workflow. Keep the Runtime, Editor, Samples, and Documentation folders together so assembly definitions and sample references remain intact.

If the required Unity packages are not already installed, add Unity UI and Input System through Window > Package Management > Package Manager.

docs.title: EventSystem setup
docs.text:
Each UI scene needs one active EventSystem configured for the New Input System:

  1. Create or select the scene's EventSystem.
  2. Use InputSystemUIInputModule as its UI input module.
  3. Assign enabled UI actions for navigation, submit, cancel, pointer position, and click as required by the project.
  4. Avoid running a legacy StandaloneInputModule on the same EventSystem.
The sample EventSystem uses InputSystemUIInputModule with Point, Click, Navigate, Submit, Cancel, and Scroll Wheel actions assigned.

Add SmartFocusManager to a suitable scene object. Assign its Event System field explicitly, or leave it empty to use EventSystem.current. Explicit assignment is preferable in scenes with unusual initialization order.

To use input-mode-aware focus policy, add SmartInputModeDetector and assign the same UI action references used by InputSystemUIInputModule. The detector observes those actions; it does not enable or disable them.

docs.title: Input System project setting
docs.text: The project's active input handling must support the New Input System. Smart UI Focus & Navigation does not modify this or any other global project setting automatically.

docs.title: Layout constraints
docs.text:
SmartNavigationLayoutConstraint describes the directional topology of descendant controls within a SmartNavigationGroup. Set its Topology in the Inspector or through the public property.

The nearest active constraint between a Selectable and its navigation group applies to that control.

docs.title: Freeform
docs.text: Freeform allows all directions and uses the group's bounds-aware spatial scoring. Use it for irregular or mixed layouts that do not have strict row/column structure.

docs.title: VerticalList
docs.text: VerticalList allows Up and Down from constrained descendants. Left and Right resolve to no target, including at the list boundary. This prevents a single-column list from escaping horizontally into nearby controls.

docs.title: HorizontalList
docs.text: HorizontalList allows Left and Right from constrained descendants. Up and Down resolve to no target.

docs.title: Grid
docs.text:
Grid derives directional neighbors from visual row and column lanes and overlapping screen-space bounds. Horizontal navigation stays within the source row, and vertical navigation stays within the source column.

At a grid boundary, the group can still consider a sensible external control outside the constraint when it shares the relevant visual lane.

docs.title: Ragged grid example
docs.text:
1  2  3
4  5  6
7  8

From Item 8, Right has no internal target because no third item exists in that row. It does not jump diagonally to Item 6 in the previous row. Likewise, Item 6 has no internal Down target because the third column does not continue into the final row.

This behavior defines the Smart Grid topology; it is not a claim that every Unity Automatic grid produces an incorrect result.

docs.title: Changing topology at runtime
docs.text:
Assigning Topology marks the owning group dirty. With automatic rebuilding enabled, the new topology is applied before a later canvas render. Otherwise, update the layout first and call RebuildNavigation() yourself.

layoutConstraint.Topology = SmartNavigationTopology.Grid;
navigationGroup.MarkNavigationDirty();

docs.title: Modals
docs.text: SmartFocusManager uses a focus stack for modal and popup flows. The application remains responsible for opening, closing, and identifying modal panels.

docs.title: Open a modal
docs.text:
1. Ensure the base menu scope is current and its opener is selected.
  2. Activate the modal GameObject.
  3. Call PushModal with the active modal scope.

The manager records the current base scope and its exact valid selection, then focuses the modal scope using its remembered/default/fallback order.

docs.title: Close a modal
docs.text:
1. Deactivate or otherwise close the modal UI.
  2. Call PopModal.

If the saved base selection remains valid, it is restored exactly. Otherwise, the manager resolves the base scope's normal focus target.

Your browser does not support embedded video. Open the modal restoration demonstration. The modal receives focus while open, then the exact valid opener is restored when it closes. 
using LevelArgento.SmartUINavigation;
using UnityEngine;

public sealed class PopupController : MonoBehaviour
{
    [SerializeField] private SmartFocusManager focusManager;
    [SerializeField] private GameObject popup;
    [SerializeField] private SmartFocusScope popupScope;

    public void Open()
    {
        popup.SetActive(true);
        focusManager.PushModal(popupScope);
    }

    public void Close()
    {
        popup.SetActive(false);
        focusManager.PopModal();
    }
}

The modal scope passed to PushModal must exist and be active and enabled; otherwise, the method returns false. PopModal returns false when no restoration entry exists.

Calling SetScope, including SetScope(null), clears the modal restoration stack. Do not use SetScope to enter a popup when opener restoration is required.

The manager does not discover third-party or application-specific modal systems automatically. Integrate their open/close events with PushModal and PopModal, and make sure asynchronous close logic calls PopModal at the intended time.

docs.title: Navigation overrides
docs.text:
Add SmartNavigationOverride to a GameObject that already has a Selectable to replace individual directions after the owning SmartNavigationGroup calculates its normal links.

Each of Up, Down, Left, and Right has one mode.

docs.title: Auto
docs.text: Auto preserves the target generated by the navigation group.

docs.title: None
docs.text: None forces the direction to have no target.

docs.title: Explicit
docs.text:
Explicit uses the assigned Selectable only when that target is active, enabled, and interactable at rebuild time. The target may be outside the navigation group.

If the assigned target is missing or invalid, the direction resolves to no target. It does not fall back to the generated Auto target.

docs.title: Inspector
docs.text:
The custom Inspector shows a mode field for each direction. Explicit Target appears only when that direction uses Explicit mode. Changing a serialized override in the Inspector marks the owning group dirty through normal Unity validation.

The sample Profile control blocks Up, explicitly targets Apply on Left, and leaves Down and Right on Auto.

docs.title: Runtime configuration
docs.text:
using LevelArgento.SmartUINavigation;
using UnityEngine;
using UnityEngine.UI;

public sealed class NavigationOverrideSetup : MonoBehaviour
{
    [SerializeField] private SmartNavigationOverride navigationOverride;
    [SerializeField] private Selectable explicitLeftTarget;

    public void Configure()
    {
        navigationOverride.Up = new SmartNavigationDirectionOverride(
            SmartNavigationOverrideMode.None);

        navigationOverride.Left = new SmartNavigationDirectionOverride(
            SmartNavigationOverrideMode.Explicit,
            explicitLeftTarget);
    }
}

Setting a public direction property marks the owning group dirty. With automatic rebuilding disabled, call RebuildNavigation() on the group after configuring overrides.

docs.title: Sample scene
docs.text: Two samples are included: the technical Focus Management Sample below and the polished game-menu Navigation Showcase.

docs.title: Focus Management Sample
docs.text:
Open:

Assets/LevelArgento/SmartUINavigation/Samples/FocusManagement/FocusManagementSample.unity

The scene includes an EventSystem, InputSystemUIInputModule, input actions, focus components, navigation components, and a camera. Enter Play Mode to exercise the runtime behavior.

The sample controller connects the focus manager, input-mode detector, scopes, panels, modal, and recovery controls.

docs.title: Controls
docs.text:
• Arrow keys, D-pad, or left stick: navigate.
  • Enter or gamepad south button: submit.
  • Mouse movement and clicks: pointer interaction and mode switching.

The footer displays the current Mouse, Keyboard, or Gamepad input mode.

docs.title: Main Menu
docs.text:
The Options button receives default focus when Play Mode starts. Move to another Main Menu control, enter another panel, and return to observe per-scope selection memory.

Open Modal Popup, then close it. Focus returns to the exact Main Menu control that opened the popup while that control remains valid.

docs.title: Options / recovery
docs.text:
To verify remembered selection without selecting Back first:

  1. Open Options, navigate to Disable My Button Component, and leave it selected for at least one frame without submitting it.
  2. From code, call the sample controller's public ShowMainMenu() method directly. This leaves the Options scope without changing EventSystem selection to Back first.
  3. Call ShowOptions() directly in the same way.
  4. Confirm that Disable My Button Component, rather than the default control, is selected again.

Use the first three demonstration buttons in order. They make the current selection non-interactable, disable its Button component, or deactivate its GameObject. In keyboard or gamepad mode, the focus manager recovers to another valid control. Reset Recovery Buttons restores the demonstration controls.

docs.title: Smart Navigation
docs.text:
This section uses an intentionally irregular arrangement. Navigate in all four directions to inspect the generated, bounds-aware routes.

The Profile control demonstrates manual overrides:

  • Up is None.
  • Left is Explicit to Apply.
  • Down and Right remain Auto.

docs.title: Dynamic Navigation
docs.text:
The dynamic section generates eight item buttons at runtime. Use its toolbar to:

  • add or remove an item;
  • disable or re-enable an item;
  • shuffle sibling order; and
  • switch between a one-column vertical list and a three-column grid.

Navigate after each change. Invalid controls are skipped, links follow the updated visual layout, and the ragged final grid row keeps its row/column boundaries. Submitting a generated item removes it and demonstrates focus recovery.

Your browser does not support embedded video. Open the Dynamic Navigation walkthrough. The Dynamic Navigation panel demonstrates runtime content and topology changes in the included scene.

docs.title: Suggested device pass
docs.text:
1. Start with keyboard and visit every panel.
  2. Repeat with a gamepad, including left-stick and D-pad input.
  3. Move and click the mouse, then return to keyboard or gamepad input.
  4. Confirm the footer mode changes and focus remains usable according to the active input mode.

docs.title: Navigation Showcase
docs.text:
Open Assets/LevelArgento/SmartUINavigation/Samples/NavigationShowcase/NavigationShowcase.unity for a black-and-orange game menu with a runtime-generated, three-column Dynamic Navigation panel. It demonstrates focus recovery, remembered selection, modal restoration, ragged-grid navigation, dynamic rebuilding, and input mode detection.

Navigation Showcase — polished game-menu layout and dynamic navigation panel.
  • Play receives default focus in the vertical menu. Navigate with arrow keys, D-pad, or left stick; move Right to enter the dynamic area. Continue is intentionally non-interactable.
  • Profile demonstrates direction overrides: Left is None, Up is Explicit to Settings, and Down/Right remain Auto.
  • The dynamic grid starts with five items. Add Item creates another selectable, up to nine visible items. Reorder swaps alternating adjacent pairs in the actual sibling order, moving items through middle positions as well as both ends. Reset restarts this deterministic sequence. Navigation rebuilds from the updated layout; incomplete rows retain their column boundaries.
  • Remove Item removes the last selected grid item (initially Item 01). Delete removes the currently focused item without first selecting a toolbar button. The count and brief Navigation Rebuilt notice reflect each change.
  • Click or focus a grid item, then use Disable Item in Focus Recovery. The sample targets the remembered item, not the command button. Disabling or removing selects the next valid item in the current grid order, or the nearest valid predecessor when none follows. Repeated disabling stays in the grid until no valid items remain; only then does the sample request normal scope fallback. This local selection uses the manager's public APIs without changing its global recovery policy. Enable Item restores the most recently disabled item still waiting, including its focus. The status shows the next item to restore and how many remain, or No Disabled Items. Removing an item clears its pending restoration; Reset clears all pending restorations. D also disables a focused menu or grid item.
Focus Recovery — disabling the selected item keeps focus on another valid control.
  • The Continue status and Enable / Disable action control the initially unavailable menu button. No save-game state is involved.
  • Open Settings, choose Audio, Video or Controls, then Close Settings and reopen it. The scope restores the exact previous option. The close button is outside the remembered scope and does not replace that option. Esc / gamepad east or L also closes Settings; R reopens it.
  • From the main scope, L or Esc / gamepad east still leaves the menu. R or Return To Menu restores its remembered selection.
  • Open Modal, M, or any available menu option other than Settings opens the modal. Cancel or confirm restores the exact opener. Esc / gamepad east also closes it. Menu options do not launch a game or quit the application.
  • Reset restores the original five items in order, re-enables demonstration controls, and selects Play. The footer shows the current input mode, selected control, and shortcuts; mouse and touch use the shared sample UI actions.

This scene reuses the FocusManagement sample's Input Actions, rounded sprite, audio, and feedback components. Keep both sample folders when using it.

docs.title: Smart navigation
docs.text:
SmartNavigationGroup generates Up, Down, Left, and Right targets for uGUI Selectable controls beneath it. It uses current screen-space RectTransform bounds to prefer candidates in the requested direction with sensible alignment and proximity.

The result is deterministic for the same hierarchy and layout. It is intended for irregular menus and structured layouts where explicit, reproducible links are preferable to Unity's runtime Automatic mode. Ordinary menus may work equally well with Unity's built-in navigation.

Your browser does not support embedded video. Open the smart navigation demonstration. The sample's irregular layout keeps directional movement deliberate across staggered controls.

docs.title: Participants
docs.text:
A participant must:

  • be a descendant of the group;
  • use a RectTransform;
  • be active and enabled;
  • be interactable; and
  • not belong to a nested SmartNavigationGroup.

Invalid controls are excluded as navigation targets. Transition settings, colors, animation triggers, and target graphics are not changed.

docs.title: Generated links are Explicit
docs.text:
RebuildNavigation() calculates all four directions, applies any active manual overrides, and writes the result to each participant's Selectable.navigation property using Navigation.Mode.Explicit.

This replaces the participant's previous navigation mode and directional targets. It does not permanently modify unrelated controls outside the group. A control removed from the group can retain navigation that was previously written directly onto that control; reset or rebuild it elsewhere if that matters to the application.

docs.title: Rebuilding
docs.text:
RebuildAutomatically is enabled by default. The group marks itself dirty for relevant hierarchy, layout, validity, and transform changes, then rebuilds before a later canvas render.

Use the public methods when coordinating custom UI code:

navigationGroup.MarkNavigationDirty();

MarkNavigationDirty() schedules an automatic rebuild only while RebuildAutomatically is enabled. If automatic rebuilding is disabled, call:

navigationGroup.RebuildNavigation();

The component also exposes Rebuild Navigation in its context menu.

For runtime-generated layouts, allow Unity's layout system to update positions before rebuilding. See dynamic UI.

docs.title: Structured content
docs.text: Add SmartNavigationLayoutConstraint around list or grid content when its topology should control valid directions. Freeform controls continue to use spatial candidate scoring. See layout constraints.

docs.title: Support
docs.text:
Publisher: LevelArgento

Support: support@levelargento.com

When requesting support, include:

  • Unity editor version;
  • Unity UI and Input System package versions;
  • the relevant component Inspector configuration;
  • steps to reproduce the issue; and
  • Console messages or a minimal reproduction scene where practical.

docs.title: No focus when Play Mode starts
docs.text:
Symptom: No control is selected after entering Play Mode.

Likely cause: Initial Scope is unassigned or inactive, its targets are invalid, or the manager cannot resolve an EventSystem.

Fix/check: Assign an active scope and valid default child. Assign the EventSystem explicitly and confirm the EventSystem GameObject is active.

docs.title: EventSystem missing
docs.text:
Symptom: The Console reports SmartFocusManager requires an active EventSystem.

Likely cause: The manager's Event System field is empty and EventSystem.current is unavailable.

Fix/check: Add one active EventSystem to the scene and assign it to the manager.

docs.title: Input System actions not enabled
docs.text:
Symptom: CurrentMode never changes from its initial value.

Likely cause: The detector observes disabled actions, or its references do not match the active UI action map.

Fix/check: Assign the same actions used by InputSystemUIInputModule and ensure that action map is enabled. The detector does not enable actions itself.

docs.title: Gamepad does not navigate
docs.text:
Symptom: Gamepad activity may be detected, but Unity UI selection does not move.

Likely cause: The InputSystemUIInputModule Navigate action lacks the needed bindings, or no valid selection exists.

Fix/check: Verify the module's Navigate action contains D-pad or stick bindings, the action is enabled, and the active scope has a valid focus target.

docs.title: Selection disappears after panel changes
docs.text:
Symptom: Closing or deactivating a panel leaves no usable selection.

Likely cause: The application deactivated the selected panel without activating and setting the next focus scope.

Fix/check: Activate the destination panel, then call SetScope(destinationScope). Use modal APIs instead for popups that should restore an opener.

docs.title: Remembered selection is not restored
docs.text:
Symptom: Returning to a scope selects its default instead of the prior control.

Likely cause: Remember Last Selection is disabled, memory was cleared, or the remembered control is no longer valid.

Fix/check: Enable scope memory and confirm the control remains a descendant, active, enabled, and interactable. Invalid memory intentionally falls through to the default.

docs.title: Modal focus does not return
docs.text:
Symptom: Closing a popup does not restore the base menu selection.

Likely cause: The popup was entered with SetScope, SetScope was called while it was open, or PopModal was not called.

Fix/check: Open with PushModal and close with PopModal. Avoid SetScope during that modal stack because it clears restoration history.

docs.title: Navigation does not rebuild after a custom runtime layout change
docs.text:
Symptom: Links still follow old positions or old content.

Likely cause: The rebuild ran before layout settled, or automatic rebuilding is disabled.

Fix/check: Mark the layout and group dirty for a deferred rebuild. For an immediate result, call LayoutRebuilder.ForceRebuildLayoutImmediate before RebuildNavigation().

docs.title: Explicit override produces no target
docs.text:
Symptom: A direction configured as Explicit does nothing.

Likely cause: Its target is missing, inactive, disabled, or non-interactable.

Fix/check: Assign a valid Selectable and rebuild. Invalid Explicit targets resolve to no target and do not fall back to Auto.

docs.title: Mouse and gamepad behavior differs from expectation
docs.text:
Symptom: Focus is not recovered during mouse use, or selection recovers more aggressively without a detector.

Likely cause: This is the manager's current input-mode policy.

Fix/check: Assign and configure SmartInputModeDetector when Mouse mode should pause recovery. Verify pointer, click, navigation, submit, and cancel references use the active UI action map.
